12:1: Alif Lam Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.
12:2: Indeed, We sent it down as an Arabic Quran so that you may reason.
12:3: We narrate to you the best of stories by revealing to you this Quran. Whereas before this you were certainly among the unaware.
12:4: When Joseph said to his father: 'O my father, I saw eleven stars, the sun, and the moon. I saw them prostrating to me.'
12:5: He said: 'O my son, do not relate your dream to your brothers, lest they plot a trap against you. Indeed, Satan is a clear enemy to man.'
12:6: And thus your Rabb will choose you, teach you the interpretation of events, and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob, just as He completed it before upon your forefathers Abraham and Isaac; indeed, your Rabb is al-Alim, al-Hakim.
12:7: Certainly, in Joseph and his brothers there are signs for those who ask.
12:8: They said: "Joseph and his brother are more beloved to our father than us, whereas we are a group. Indeed, our father is in clear error."
12:9: Kill Joseph or cast him to a place so that your father's face may remain for you, and after that you may become a righteous group.
12:10: A speaker from among them said: Do not kill Joseph, leave him at the bottom of the well so that some travelers may pick him up, if you are to do so.
12:11: They said: 'O our father, what is the matter with you that you do not trust us with Joseph? Whereas we are indeed well-wishers for him.'
12:12: Send him with us tomorrow, let him enjoy himself and play, and indeed, we will protect him.
12:13: He said: "Indeed, taking him away saddens me, and I fear that a wolf might eat him while you are unaware of him."
12:14: They said: If a wolf eats him while we are a group, indeed, we would then be losers.
12:15: When they took him away and resolved to cast him into the bottom of the well, We revealed to him: 'You will surely inform them of this deed of theirs.'
12:16: And they came to their father in the evening, weeping.
12:17: They said: O our father! We were racing and left Joseph by our belongings, and a wolf ate him. But you will not believe us, even if we are truthful.
12:18: And they came with false blood upon his shirt. He said: Nay, your souls have enticed you to a matter. So patience is beautiful! And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe.
12:19: A caravan arrived and they sent their water drawer. And he let down his bucket. He said: Good news! This is a boy! And they hid him as merchandise. Allah is the Knower of what they do.
12:20: They sold him for a small price, for counted dirhams, and they were among those reluctant regarding him.
12:21: And the one from Egypt who bought him said to his wife: Make his dwelling place honorable, perhaps he will benefit us or we may adopt him as a child. And thus We established Joseph in the land, and that We might teach him of the interpretation of hadiths. And Allah is dominant over His affair, but most of the people do not know.
12:22: And when he reached his maturity, We gave him judgment and knowledge, and thus We reward the doers of good.
12:23: The woman in whose house he was sought him for herself. She locked the doors and said: Come on, to you! He said: I seek refuge in Allah! Indeed, he is my master, he made my dwelling good. Indeed, the wrongdoers do not attain salvation.
12:24: And certainly she desired him, and he would have desired her had he not seen the proof of his Rabb; thus it was, to avert evil and indecency from him.
12:25: They both raced to the door. She tore his shirt from behind. By the door they found her master. She said: What is the penalty for one who intended evil for your family, except to be imprisoned or a painful punishment?
12:26: He said: She sought me for herself. A witness from her family testified: If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has spoken the truth and he is among the liars.
12:27: And if his shirt is torn from behind, she has lied and he is among the truthful.
12:28: When he saw that his shirt was torn from behind, he said: Indeed, this is from your plot. Indeed, your plot is great.
12:29: Joseph, turn away from this, and you, ask forgiveness for your sin, because you were among the sinners.
12:30: The women in the city said: The wife of al-Aziz is seeking her young servant for herself. Love has passionately enraptured her. Indeed, we see her in clear misguidance.
12:31: When she heard their plotting, she sent for them, prepared a reclining place for them, gave each one of them a knife, and said: Come out before them.
12:32: She said: This is the one about whom you blamed me. And certainly I sought him for myself, but he guarded himself. And if he does not do what I command him, he will surely be imprisoned and will surely be among the disgraced.
12:33: He said: My Rabb! Prison is dearer to me than that to which they invite me. If You do not turn away their plot from me, I will incline toward them and be among the ignorant.
12:34: His Rabb answered him and turned away their plot from him; indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
12:35: Then after they had seen the signs, it appeared best to them to imprison him for a time.
12:36: And two young men entered the prison with him. One of them said: In my dream I see myself pressing wine. The other said: I too see in my dream that I am carrying bread upon my head from which the birds eat. Inform us of its interpretation. Indeed, we see you among the doers of good.
12:37: He said: No food that comes to you as provision shall come to you except that I have informed you of its interpretation before it comes to you. This is from what my Rabb has taught me. Indeed, I have abandoned the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah and who deny the Hereafter.
12:38: And I followed the religion of my forefathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It is not for us to associate anything with Allah. This is from Allah's favor upon us and upon people, but most of the people do not give thanks.
12:39: O my fellow prisoners, are separate lords better or Allah, the One, the Subduer?
12:40: Those you worship besides Him are nothing but names that you and your forefathers have named; Allah has sent down no authority concerning them; judgment belongs only to Allah; He has commanded that you worship none but Him; that is the upright religion, but most of the people do not know.
12:41: O my fellow prisoners! One of you will serve wine to his master, while the other will be crucified and the birds will eat from his head. The matter concerning which you inquired has been decreed.
12:42: And he said to the one of them whom he thought would be saved: Mention me before your Rabb. But Satan made him forget the mention of his Rabb. So he remained in prison for several years.
12:43: The king said: I see in my dream seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean cows, and seven green ears of grain and seven other dry ears. O eminent ones! If you interpret dreams, give me a ruling concerning my dream.
12:44: They said: Confused dreams. And we are not knowers of the interpretation of dreams.
12:45: And the one of the two who was saved and remembered after a period of time said: I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me.
12:46: Joseph, O truthful one, give us a ruling concerning seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean cows, and seven green ears of grain and seven other dry ears. That I may return to the people, perhaps they will know.
12:47: He said: You shall sow for seven years, then what you harvest, leave it in its ear, except a small part.
12:48: Then after that will come seven severe years; you will eat what you prepared beforehand, except a small part of what you save in those years.
12:49: Then after that will come a year in which the people will be given rain and in which they will press and milk.
12:50: The king said: Bring him to me. When the messenger came to him, he said: Return to your master and ask him what is the condition of the women who cut their hands. Surely my Rabb knows their plot.
12:51: He said: What was your condition when you sought Joseph from his self? They said: Far be it, for Allah! We know of no evil regarding him. The vizier's wife said: Now the truth has come to light; I sought him from his self, and he is surely of the truthful.
12:52: This is so that he may know that I did not betray him in his absence, and surely Allah does not bring the plot of the traitors to success.
12:53: I do not acquit my self, for the self is an enjoiner of evil, except for those upon whom my Rabb has mercy. Surely my Rabb is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
12:54: The ruler said: Bring him to me, that I may dedicate him to myself. When he spoke with him, he said: Surely today you possess a firm and trusted position before us.
12:55: He said: Appoint me over the storehouses of the earth; for I am a guardian and knowledgeable.
12:56: And thus We established Joseph in the land; he settles therein wherever he wills. We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will. And We do not waste the reward of the good-doers.
12:57: And the reward of the Hereafter is certainly better for those who believe and guard against evil.
12:58: The brothers of Joseph came and entered before him; he recognized them, but they did not recognize him.
12:59: When he prepared their provisions, he said: Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts?
12:60: If you do not bring him to me, then there is no measure for you with me, and do not come near me.
12:61: They said: We will turn his father away from him, and surely we have become doers.
12:62: And he said to his young men: Put their merchandise inside their loads, perhaps they will recognize it when they return to their families, perhaps they will return.
12:63: When they returned to their father, they said: O our father, measure has been denied to us, so send our brother with us that we may get measure, and we will surely protect him.
12:64: He said: Shall I trust you with him as I trusted you with his brother before? Allah is the best protector, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.
12:65: When they opened their loads, they found that their merchandise had been returned to them. They said: O our father, what more do we desire? Here is our merchandise, returned to us. We will bring food for our family, protect our brother, and add a camel's load more. This is an easy measure.
12:66: He said: I will not send him with you until you give me a firm pledge by Allah, unless you are surrounded. When they gave him their pledge, he said: Allah is Guardian over what we have said.
12:67: And he said: O my sons, do not enter from a single gate, enter from separate gates. And I cannot avail you against Allah in anything. Judgment is only for Allah. Upon Him I have relied. And let those who rely, rely upon Him alone.
12:68: And when they entered from where their father had commanded them, this was not to avail them anything before Allah, except that it satisfied a need in the self of Jacob. And surely he knows what We taught him, but most of the people do not know.
12:69: When they entered before Joseph, he embraced his brother to his chest and said: Surely I am your brother; do not grieve over what they have been doing.
12:70: When he prepared their loads, he placed the drinking cup into his brother's load. Then an announcer called out: O caravan, surely you are thieves.
12:71: They said, coming upon them, and asked: What are you missing?
12:72: They said: "We are missing the drinking cup of the king, and for the one who brings it there is a camel's load, and I am a guarantor for it."
12:73: By Allah, you know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and we were not thieves.
12:74: They said: "If you are liars, what is its penalty?"
12:75: They said its penalty: in whose load it is found, then he is its penalty; thus we penalize the wrongdoers.
12:76: So he began with their containers before his brother's container; then he brought it out of his brother's container. Thus did We arrange for Joseph. It was not for him to take his brother in the religion of the king, except that Allah willed. We raise by degrees whom We will. And above every possessor of knowledge there is One who knows.
12:77: They said: "If he has stolen, a brother of his had stolen before." Joseph hid this within himself and did not disclose it to them. He said: "You are in a worse position. Allah knows best what you describe."
12:78: They said: "O Aziz! He has a very old father. Therefore take one of us in his place. Surely we see you among the good-doers."
12:79: He said: "Allah forbid that we take other than the one with whom we found our possession. In that case, we would truly be among the wrongdoers."
12:80: When they despaired of him, they withdrew aside, conferring in whispers. Their eldest said: "Do you not know that your father took a pledge from you in the name of Allah, and the shortcoming you committed before regarding Joseph? I will not leave this place until my father permits me or Allah judges for me. And He is the best of judges."
12:81: Return to your father and say: "O our father! Surely your son committed theft, and we did not testify except to what we knew, and we were not guardians of the unseen.
12:82: And ask the town in which we were and the caravan with which we came, and surely we are truthful."
12:83: He said: "Rather, your souls have made a matter seem pleasing to you. Now, a beautiful patience. It may be that Allah will bring them all to me. Surely He is the All-Knowing, the Possessor of judgment and wisdom."
12:84: He turned away from them and said: "Alas for my grief over Joseph!" His eyes turned completely white from sorrow, and he was swallowing his anger.
12:85: They said: "By Allah, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become exhausted or become of those who perish."
12:86: He said: "I only complain of my grief and my sorrow to Allah, and I know from Allah that which you do not know."
12:87: O my sons! Go and search for Joseph and his brother, and do not despair of Allah's mercy; because none despairs of Allah's mercy except the company of the disbelievers.
12:88: When they entered into his presence, they said: "O Aziz! Harm has touched us and our family, and we have come with merchandise of little worth. Give us full measure and give us charity. Surely Allah rewards the givers of charity."
12:89: He said: "Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?"
12:90: They said: "Are you Joseph?" He said: "I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has bestowed favor upon us. Surely whoever is God-fearing and patient, Allah does not waste the reward of the doers of good."
12:91: They said: "By Allah, Allah has truly preferred you over us. And indeed, we were sinners."
12:92: He said: "There is no blame upon you today. Allah will forgive you. And He is the Most Merciful of the merciful."
12:93: Take this shirt of mine, cast it over my father's face, his eyes will become seeing, and bring your whole family to me.
12:94: When the caravan departed, their father said: "Surely I perceive the scent of Joseph, if you do not think me senile."
12:95: They said: "By Allah for you, surely you are in your old error."
12:96: When the bearer of good news came, he cast it over his face, and immediately he became seeing. He said: "Did I not tell you that I know from Allah what you do not know?"
12:97: They said: "O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins for us; surely we were sinners."
12:98: He said: "Soon I will ask forgiveness for you of my Rabb; surely He Himself is Most Forgiving and Rahim."
12:99: When they entered into the presence of Joseph, he took his mother and father to himself and said: "Enter Egypt in safety, if Allah wills."
12:100: And he raised his mother and father onto the throne, and they fell down prostrating to him. He said: "O my father, this is the interpretation of my dream that I saw before. My Rabb has made it true. And He was good to me when He brought me out of the prison and brought you from the desert after Satan had caused discord between me and my brothers. Surely my Rabb is gracious to whom He wills. Surely He is the All-Knowing, the Possessor of wisdom."
12:101: My Rabb! Indeed, You have given me of the dominion and taught me the interpretation of dreams. O Creator of the heavens and the earth! You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
12:102: That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. And you were not with them when they combined their affairs and while they were plotting.
12:103: And most of the people, however intensely you desire, are not believers.
12:104: You do not ask them for any reward in return for this; it is only a reminder for the worlds.
12:105: And how many a sign there is in the heavens and the earth, which they pass by while turning away from it.
12:106: And most of them do not believe in Allah except while associating partners.
12:107: Or did they feel secure that an overwhelming disaster from the punishment of Allah would come upon them, or that the Hour would come upon them at a moment when they are unaware?
12:108: Say: "This is my way. I and those who follow me invite to Allah upon insight. Allah is exalted and I am not of the polytheists."
12:109: And before you We did not send except men from the people of the cities to whom We revealed. Have they not traveled in the earth and seen how the end of those before them was? And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who are God-fearing. Will you still not reason?
12:110: Until, when the messengers fell into despair and thought that they were denied, Our help came to them and whoever We willed was saved. And Our battle is not turned away from the guilty people.
12:111: Certainly, in their stories there is a lesson for the possessors of intellect. This is not an invented statement, but a confirmation of that which was before it, and an explanation of everything, and a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe.
